title: I finally built a strategy that actually wins and I STILL almost blew up my account. Turns out the edge was never my problem. My bet size was.
author: Electronic_Tea_2948
selftext:
This one still embarrasses me a little. After months of building junk, I finally had a strategy with a genuine, real, positive edge. Backtested clean, held up out of sample, the whole thing. I was so sure of it that when I went live I sized way up, because why wouldn't you press a winner, right?  
Then it hit a completely normal losing streak. Nothing weird, nothing broken, just the ordinary run of losers that every strategy has baked into it. And because I'd bet so big per trade, that ordinary streak carved something like a third of my account off in a couple of weeks. I sat there genuinely confused, because the strategy was doing exactly what it was supposed to do. It was winning over time. I was just betting so heavily that a normal cold patch nearly ended me before the edge could show up.  
That sent me down the position sizing rabbit hole and honestly it reframed everything for me. The big thing that broke my brain is that you can have a real, positive-expectancy strategy and still go broke purely from betting too much per trade. The edge tells you that you win in the long run. Your bet size decides whether you survive long enough to get there. Those are two totally separate problems and I'd only been thinking about the first one.  
The other thing that got me was learning there's a mathematically optimal bet size for growing an account, and that betting bigger than that is not just riskier, it actually grows your account slower too. Past a certain point you're getting more pain and less reward at the same time, which feels insane until you sit with it. And even that "optimal" size produces drawdowns most humans can't emotionally stomach, which is why a lot of people deliberately bet a fraction of it. I now size way smaller than my gut wants to, scaled to how volatile the thing I'm trading is, and my equity curve finally stopped trying to give me a heart attack.  
So the question I keep chewing on for you all. How do you actually size? Fixed fraction, volatility-based, some fraction of the optimal, flat risk per trade? And has anyone else had the specific gut punch of watching a genuinely good strategy nearly kill you just because you bet too fat? I feel like sizing is where most of us quietly die and nobody talks about it as much as the entry signals.

comments.author: misterRegime
comments.body:
The part people skip is that the optimal size is computed from an edge you estimated, and the estimate is always noisier than the formula assumes. Overstate your edge by a bit and the optimal size overstates by a lot, so betting a fraction of it isn't really squeamishness, it's paying for the fact that you don't know your own numbers as well as the maths pretends.

My constraint ended up being concurrency rather than per-trade size. When several positions can be open at once, the thing that hurts isn't one big loss, it's four correlated ones landing together, and sizing each trade in isolation doesn't see that at all. Worth checking whether your losing streak was really a streak or several overlapping positions going wrong at the same time, because they need different fixes.

comments.author: AdBitter6080
comments.body: Edge and sizing are two separate problems, and confusing them is how profitable systems still go broke. Your edge tells you the expected value per trade; your bet size determines whether you survive the ordinary cold streaks long enough for that edge to show up. The mathematically right move is to size to a fraction of full-Kelly, usually 10-25%, so a normal drawdown does not force you out before the mean reverts. Rule of thumb: if a losing streak keeps you up at night, you are betting too big; cut size until the worst historical drawdown feels boring.
